headline: Bijoya Dashami: Durga Puja concludes with idol immersion on Wednesday
summary: Devotees across Bangladesh celebrate the final day of the Sharadiya Durga Puja festival with traditional rituals and farewells.
details: The largest religious festival of the Hindu community, Sharadiya Durga Puja, concludes this Wednesday, October 21, with the immersion of idols in water bodies.
Since morning, various puja mandaps across the country have been buzzing with religious rituals, prayers, and the offering of anjali.
Devotees of all ages have participated in the celebrations, with prasad being distributed at various mandaps after the completion of the puja.
Special rituals for Dashami Puja include offering betel leaves, betel nuts, and water lilies to the goddess's hands.
Women devotees have also participated in the traditional 'Sindur Khela' (vermilion play) as part of the final festivities.
Beyond the religious ceremonies, many are spending the day meeting relatives and acquaintances to exchange greetings and spend time together.
Following the completion of all formal rituals, the idols will be immersed in designated water bodies to mark the end of the festival.
caption:
The bells of farewell ring across Bangladesh as the grand Sharadiya Durga Puja festival concludes today.

The largest religious festival of the Hindu community, Sharadiya Durga Puja, concludes this Wednesday, October 21, with the immersion of idols in water bodies.

Since morning, various puja mandaps across the country have been buzzing with religious rituals, prayers, and the offering of anjali.

Devotees of all ages have participated in the celebrations, with prasad being distributed at various mandaps after the completion of the puja.

Special rituals for Dashami Puja include offering betel leaves, betel nuts, and water lilies to the goddess's hands.

Women devotees have also participated in the traditional 'Sindur Khela' (vermilion play) as part of the final festivities.

Beyond the religious ceremonies, many are spending the day meeting relatives and acquaintances to exchange greetings and spend time together.

Following the completion of all formal rituals, the idols will be immersed in designated water bodies to mark the end of the festival.

headline_marked: Teenager [[beaten to death over theft accusation]] in Jessore
headline: Teenager beaten to death over theft accusation in Jessore
summary: The victim, Swadhin Mia, died in a Dhaka hospital on Tuesday after being severely beaten by a group of people on Saturday night.
details: A teenager named Swadhin Mia, a resident of Barandipara Mollapara in Jessore city, has been killed after being beaten by a group of people over theft accusations.
The incident occurred on Saturday night in Malopara, where Swadhin was allegedly beaten severely, resulting in critical head injuries.
Following the initial treatment at a local hospital, he was shifted to a private hospital in Dhaka for advanced care, but he passed away on Tuesday afternoon.
The victim's father has accused local residents, including individuals named Shahidul and Ujjwal, of planning the attack on his son.
The body of the teenager has been sent to the Jessore General Hospital morgue for an autopsy to determine the exact cause of death.
Police have stated that that they will take legal action after receiving a formal complaint and conducting a thorough investigation into the incident.
